title: 3. Authentication Attacks (A07)
objective: Study-guide review — ICCS423 v2 — L10: Web Security 1 (Injection · Auth · Access Control · Sessions): 3. Authentication Attacks (A07).

items: Credential Stuffing — replay leaked username/password pairs (works due to password reuse)
Brute Force — sequential password guessing; mitigated by rate-limit + lockout
Password Spraying — one weak password across many accounts (evades per-account lockout)
Default Credentials — admin/admin still everywhere in IoT/OT
MFA Bypass — push-bombing fatigue, SIM swap, OTP phishing, recovery flow abuse
Strong password storage: Argon2id (preferred) or bcrypt; never MD5/SHA1
Have I Been Pwned API — block known-breached passwords on signup
Rate limiting — per IP and per account; exponential backoff
Account lockout — temporary, with secure recovery (not security questions)

blocks.text: ``python # ✅ Argon2id password hashing from argon2 import PasswordHasher ph = PasswordHasher(time_cost=2, memory_cost=65536, parallelism=2) hashed = ph.hash(password) ph.verify(hashed, provided_password) ``

Credential stuffing is a numbers game: attackers feed millions of leaked email/password pairs through automation. The defense is layered — block known-breached passwords (HIBP), require MFA on sensitive operations, monitor anomalous login patterns. MFA fatigue (Uber 2022) shows MFA is not magic — push notifications without number-matching are a known weakness.
